title: In vivo feasibility study of humanoid robots in surgery.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py: Europe PMC has no full text, no supplement, no accessions, no NCBI links. Zenodo API search found one record by the first author (10.5281/zenodo.18023650, 'Laparoscopic Humanoid Code'), resource type 'software', CC-BY-4.0, single file g1_teleoperate-lap_surgie.zip (80.5 MB, above the 50 MB cap, so not downloaded). Nature article page redirects to a login, so not read.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the arXiv preprint (2607.07972) via WebFetch: the availability statement names only the Zenodo code deposit; dry-lab user studies had 18 participants (O-ring transfer, 6 trials each across 3 platforms) and 13 participants (FLS, Fundamentals of Laparoscopic Surgery, peg transfer); outcomes are completion time, weighted error scores and Likert workload surveys; in vivo arm is 2 pig gallbladder removals. No released kinematics, video or per-trial table is mentioned.

a1_downloadable.note: Only a software zip is deposited (Zenodo, 80.5 MB, labelled 'software'); the paper names no data deposit. Per-trial measurements and robot recordings are not released as far as the preprint text shows; file contents not opened (over size cap).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No released table with a label column; task times and error scores exist only as figures/summary statistics in the paper (paper text only).

a3_inputs_present.note: No inputs (kinematic traces, video) are released as data, per the preprint's availability statement.

a5_enough_rows.note: Even if released, the user studies are roughly 18 x 6 = 108 O-ring trials plus 13 FLS participants and 2 pig surgeries (paper text), far under the 400-row classification floor.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; only an 80.5 MB code zip exists

a8_label_provenance.note: Completion times and error scores would be direct measurements, but they are not released.

honest_claim_h3: No ML claim is possible: the paper is an engineering feasibility study with about 31 human participants and 2 pig surgeries, and only its teleoperation code is released.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use robot-arm motion recordings from surgical training tasks to predict task time and error score.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-trial motion recordings of a teleoperated humanoid robot doing laparoscopic (keyhole-surgery) training tasks; number of trials released: unknown, likely zero (roughly 108 trials described in the paper).
plain_idea.predict: Task completion time and weighted error score, measured by the study team during the training tasks.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Automated skill scoring could help train surgeons on new robot platforms, but this paper releases no recordings and is far too small to learn it from.

ml_idea: Surgical skill or error prediction from humanoid teleoperation kinematics; not feasible because no data is released and the study has about 31 participants and 2 animals.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no dataset exists to build a table from.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the Zenodo record type and the availability statement: only software is deposited (done; project killed).

verdict_reason: Robotics engineering feasibility study, not a biology dataset: only teleoperation code is deposited on Zenodo, no per-trial data is released (A1/A2/A3 fail), and the study itself has about 31 participants and 2 pig surgeries (A5 fails).
